gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Oxanium draws its tall lowercase with rounded-rod strokes that never change width, giving the heading a distinctive, commanding look. And Noto Sans Coptic sits underneath as sans-serif text, its open s and c keeping the middle of each line full.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Oxanium runs on flat, fineliner-thin lines, with big lowercase and curves that end in clear daylight. Noto Sans Cuneiform then follows with a puffy, inflated lowercase and an e that stays open.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Crisp, uniform lines, zero stroke contrast. Oxanium makes the heading feel commanding, while Noto Sans Deseret stays friendly below with open apertures and a wide-looking lowercase.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-devanagari: Oxanium looks laser-cut, every curve and diagonal made with one cutting width and a high x-height that enlarges the lowercase. Its hard edge against Noto Sans Devanagari's compact, softer skyline is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin. Oxanium is best at announcing things with that commanding, uniform stroke, whereas Noto Sans Duployan is best at carrying text, with its wide-mouthed a and oversized, generous counters.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Oxanium writes everything with one fixed nib. It is best at drawing the eye with that distinctive uniform line, while Noto Sans Elbasan, a sans-serif with large lowercase and open terminals, is best at quietly carrying the words that follow.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Rounded-rod strokes, tall lowercase, zero fuss. Oxanium is best at grabbing attention with that single-weight build, but Noto Sans Elymaic, a sans-serif with open apertures, is best at staying out of the way afterward.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Noto Sans Ethiopic reads sturdy and tall, its c terminals hanging well away from the bowl for a modern, professional feel. Oxanium is best at commanding attention with a single line weight; the sans simply handles the text.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Oxanium's strokes feel like rope, uniform in every stem, bowl and tail. Over a longer passage, Noto Sans Georgian, a plain sans with open curves and short ascender stems, would read cleanly and move along without friction.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Oxanium's diagonals carry just as much heft as its stems, so the whole heading feels like one cut from the same bar. A longer passage in Noto Sans Glagolitic, sturdy and open, would read approachably.
